name: IL-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with a +12 partisan lean
Incumbent Brad Schneider running with a large financial advantage
Republican challenger Carl Lambrecht has no reported fundraising
model.rationale: The district's +12 Democratic lean, Schneider's incumbency and roughly $3 million raised against a challenger with no reported finances all point to a comfortable Democratic hold, and prediction markets price a Democratic win near certain. With no polls to contradict the fundamentals, the race stays at a wide Democratic margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much tighter race or unexpected outside spending against Schneider would warrant revisiting the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Brad Schneider, a Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a northern Illinois district that leans about twelve points Democratic. He has raised roughly $3 million and holds nearly $1.7 million on hand, while Republican Carl Lambrecht reports no fundraising figures, leaving Schneider with a decisive resource edge and no outside spending against him.

No general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 96 percent. The seat is expected to remain comfortably in Democratic hands in November.
